overall_summary: First-person speculative survival formats ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic environments drive the highest traction, generating Factverse's peak view counts (800-1,000+ views) and strongest engagement (up to 38 likes and comment activity). Conversely, repeatedly recycling basic psychology and generic trivia ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Why Space Is Completely Silent') consistently bottoms out with low double-digit views and near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Survival / 'What If You Fell Into' Cosmic Peril
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,028 views, 38 likes, 2 comments) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperform standard fact recitations by 5x-10x.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme astronomical and planetary phenomena as immediate, sensory, second-person survival journeys rather than textbook factoids.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Visceral Planet Attributes & Bizarre Physics
winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring stark sensory extremes like 'TrES-2b' (1,027 views, 36 likes) and 'Supersonic Rubies' (723 views, 25 likes) pull strong click-through and like ratios (>3.5%).
winning_patterns.action: Pair tactile, vivid sensory anchors (unbearable pressure, lethal radiation, extreme temperatures) with concrete astrophysics.

weak_patterns.pattern: Recycled Psychological and Everyday Body Trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' uploaded across multiple variations stalled at 5 to 53 views with 0 likes and 0 comments; earworm psychology stalled at 17-71 views.
weak_patterns.action: Halt repetitive uploads of common psychological fun-facts and earworm explanations; audiences show zero urgency or engagement.

weak_patterns.evidence: Uploading identical titles ('Why Space Is Completely Silent' across 4 uploads; 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' across 3 uploads) cannibalizes reach and results in single-digit engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication and retire repeatedly re-hashed premise scripts in favor of novel entities.

next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the cloud is colder than the background radiation of the Big Bang itself because it is an expanding cosmic refrigerator, where even light-speed thermal decay freezes atoms solid before you can scream.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-converting 'What If You Fell Into' framing at the optimal 21-second length, tapping into extreme cosmic peril while introducing a fresh, unexploited entity (Boomerang Nebula) to prevent topic fatigue.
